answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by tying each vote to a one-time admission proof-of-work plus a slowly vesting stake, then folding every key a participant holds into a single vault worth one seat. A thousand fake names no longer multiply influence: the attacker must pay a thousand separate admissions and lock a thousand stakes that stay illiquid for around a hundred epochs, while an honest agent pays once and builds reputation. Like a jade oasis veiled by a dust plume, the barrier is the real sunk cost per identity.
